epithet.en: Thane of Glamis, later King of Scotland

3.modern-en: Encounters the three witches on the heath with Banquo. Is hailed as Thane of Glamis, Thane of Cawdor, and future King. When Ross confirms the Cawdor title, he is shaken by the accuracy of the prophecy.

4.modern-en: Receives praise from Duncan, who names Malcolm as heir. Privately acknowledges that Malcolm now stands between him and the crown.

5.modern-en: Arrives home at Inverness. Lady Macbeth pushes him toward murdering Duncan, who will stay the night.

7.modern-en: Wavers about killing Duncan, listing reasons against it. Lady Macbeth shames his hesitation and outlines the plan to drug the guards. He resolves to go through with it.

8.modern-en: Sees a phantom dagger leading him toward Duncan's chamber. Waits for the bell that signals it is time to act.

9.modern-en: Returns from murdering Duncan, blood on his hands, deeply shaken. Hears a voice cry 'Sleep no more.' Refuses to return the daggers to the scene; Lady Macbeth does it for him.

10.modern-en: Puts on a show of shock when Duncan's murder is discovered. Kills the two guards, claiming it was done in a fury of loyalty. The act arouses some suspicion.

12.modern-en: Now King, he fears Banquo's nobility and the prophecy that Banquo's descendants will be kings. Hires two murderers to kill Banquo and his son Fleance.

13.modern-en: Tells Lady Macbeth that a terrible deed must be done but keeps the details from her. Hints at the plan against Banquo.

15.modern-en: At the banquet, learns Banquo is dead but Fleance escaped. Is terrified by Banquo's ghost sitting in his seat, visible only to him. His outbursts nearly expose his guilt before the assembled lords.

18.modern-en: Visits the witches and demands more prophecies. Sees three apparitions: an armed head warns him of Macduff, a bloody child says none born of woman shall harm him, and a crowned child says he is safe until Birnam Wood moves. A line of eight kings confirms Banquo's descendants will reign.

23.modern-en: Fortifies Dunsinane, relying on the prophecies. Hears that English forces approach with ten thousand men. Calls for his armor.

25.modern-en: Learns Lady Macbeth is dead and delivers the 'Tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow' speech. Then hears Birnam Wood appears to be moving — soldiers carry branches as camouflage.

27.modern-en: Fights on, killing Young Siward. Declares he bears a charmed life that no man born of woman can end.

28.modern-en: Confronts Macduff, who reveals he was ripped from his mother's womb, not born naturally. Macbeth fights on anyway and is killed. His head is brought to Malcolm.

5.modern-en: Reads Macbeth's letter about the witches' prophecy. Fears he is too full of human kindness to seize the crown. Calls on dark spirits to unsex her and fill her with cruelty. When Macbeth arrives, she takes charge of the murder plan.

6.modern-en: Welcomes Duncan to Inverness with gracious hospitality, concealing her murderous intentions.

7.modern-en: Attacks Macbeth's manhood when he hesitates about the murder. Lays out the plan to drug Duncan's guards and frame them for the killing.

9.modern-en: Waits nervously while Macbeth commits the murder. When he returns unable to function, she takes the bloody daggers back to the chamber and smears the sleeping guards with blood.

10.modern-en: Faints — or pretends to — when the murder is announced, deflecting attention from Macbeth.

12.modern-en: Invites Banquo to the evening feast, still performing the role of gracious queen.

13.modern-en: Finds no happiness in the crown. Macbeth hints at further dark deeds but keeps her in the dark about the plan against Banquo.

15.modern-en: Tries to manage Macbeth during the banquet when he sees Banquo's ghost. Dismisses the guests to prevent exposure of his guilt.

21.modern-en: Sleepwalks, rubbing her hands and reliving the murders. Cries 'Out, damned spot!' A doctor and gentlewoman observe her breakdown, concluding she needs divine help more than medicine.

3.modern-en: Witnesses the witches' prophecy alongside Macbeth. Is told he will father kings though never be one himself. Notes Macbeth's startled reaction.

4.modern-en: Present when Duncan praises Macbeth and names Malcolm as heir.

6.modern-en: Admires the pleasant setting of Inverness as he arrives with Duncan.

8.modern-en: Unable to sleep, troubled by dark thoughts about the witches' prophecy. Encounters Macbeth and uneasily agrees to discuss the prophecy later.

10.modern-en: Present when Duncan's murder is discovered. Pledges to fight against the unknown treason.

12.modern-en: Privately suspects Macbeth played foully for the crown. Accepts the invitation to Macbeth's feast and mentions he will ride out with Fleance that afternoon.

14.modern-en: Ambushed by murderers while riding with Fleance. Is killed, but Fleance escapes into the darkness.

15.modern-en: Appears as a bloody ghost at Macbeth's banquet feast, sitting in the King's seat. Visible only to Macbeth, causing him to react in terror before the lords.

6.modern-en: Arrives at Inverness with King Duncan.

10.modern-en: Discovers Duncan's murdered body and raises the alarm. His horror appears genuine and unfeigned.

11.modern-en: Refuses to attend Macbeth's coronation at Scone, already suspicious.

20.modern-en: In England, tests Malcolm's virtue by pretending to confess terrible vices. When Malcolm reveals it was a test, they unite against Macbeth. Receives devastating news that Macbeth has had his wife and children slaughtered. Swears to kill Macbeth himself.

28.modern-en: Confronts Macbeth in the final battle. Reveals he was from his mother's womb untimely ripped — not born of woman. Kills Macbeth and presents his head to Malcolm.

2.modern-en: Receives reports of the battle. Learns of Macbeth's bravery and the Thane of Cawdor's treason. Transfers the Cawdor title to Macbeth.

4.modern-en: Praises Macbeth and Banquo warmly. Names his son Malcolm as heir. Announces he will stay at Macbeth's castle in Inverness.

6.modern-en: Arrives at Inverness and is welcomed graciously by Lady Macbeth. Comments on the pleasant air around the castle — his last night alive.

epithet.en: Son of King Duncan, heir to the throne

2.modern-en: Reports to Duncan on the sergeant who saved him in battle.

4.modern-en: Named Prince of Cumberland and heir to the throne by Duncan.

10.modern-en: Flees to England after his father's murder, fearing for his life.

20.modern-en: Tests Macduff's loyalty in England by pretending to be unfit to rule. Reveals his deception and prepares to march against Macbeth with English support.

27.modern-en: Commands forces in the battle against Macbeth.

28.modern-en: Receives Macbeth's head from Macduff. Is hailed as the new King of Scotland. Promises to restore order and reward the loyal.

1.modern-en: Meet on a desolate heath amid thunder and lightning. Plan to encounter Macbeth after the battle. Chant 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair.'

3.modern-en: Greet Macbeth with three titles: Thane of Glamis, Thane of Cawdor, and future King. Tell Banquo he will father kings. Vanish into the air.

16.modern-en: Meet with Hecate, who scolds them for dealing with Macbeth without her involvement.

18.modern-en: Brew a potion in their cauldron and conjure three apparitions for Macbeth: an armed head, a bloody child, and a crowned child carrying a tree. Show a procession of eight kings descended from Banquo.

2.modern-en: Brings news of the Norwegian defeat and the Thane of Cawdor's treason to Duncan.

3.modern-en: Delivers the news that Macbeth has been named Thane of Cawdor.

6.modern-en: Arrives at Inverness with the King's party.

11.modern-en: Discusses the unnatural events surrounding Duncan's death with the Old Man.

19.modern-en: Visits Lady Macduff and tries to comfort her about her husband's flight. Leaves before the murderers arrive.

20.modern-en: Arrives in England and reluctantly tells Macduff that his wife and children have been killed.

19.modern-en: Angrily questions why Macduff has fled to England, leaving his family unprotected. Has a tender exchange with her young son. Is warned by a messenger to flee but is caught and murdered by Macbeth's assassins.

6.modern-en: Arrives with King Duncan at Inverness.

10.modern-en: Present at the discovery of Duncan's murder.

17.modern-en: Speaks sarcastically about Macbeth's increasingly suspicious actions. Discusses the hope that Macduff's mission to England will bring aid against the tyrant.

18.modern-en: Enters after the witches' apparitions and reports to Macbeth that Macduff has fled to England.

10.modern-en: Answers the knocking at the gate in a comic scene, pretending to be the porter of Hell's gate. Jokes about drink, lechery, and equivocation before admitting Macduff and Lennox.

8.modern-en: Walks with his father in the castle courtyard at night, carrying a torch.

14.modern-en: Escapes when the murderers ambush him and Banquo. His survival means the witches' prophecy about Banquo's line may still come true.

16.modern-en: Scolds the witches for dealing with Macbeth without consulting her. Instructs them to prepare more potent illusions to lure him to his destruction through overconfidence.

18.modern-en: Appears briefly to approve the witches' preparations before Macbeth arrives at the cavern.
